core_obligations: Take an element x of the fraction field integral over R and write it as a unit times a product of powers of pairwise non-associate irreducibles with integer exponents (proof lines 29823-29827).

Assume some exponent is negative and clear denominators in the integrality equation with a high power of the other primes, producing an identity that exhibits the product as divisible by the irreducible in question (proof lines 29828-29833).
Contradict uniqueness of factorization in R, so all exponents are nonnegative and x lies in R (proof lines 29833-29835).
proof_roadmap: Encode an integral element of the fraction field by its prime exponents (proof lines 29822-29827).
Rule out a negative exponent by clearing denominators and contradicting unique factorization (proof lines 29828-29836).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a unique factorization domain is normal, that is, integrally closed in its fraction field (statement lines 29817-29820). The proof does not use the theory of Dedekind domains or a minimal polynomial: it writes an integral element as a unit times a product of powers of pairwise non-associate irreducibles with integer exponents, assumes one exponent is negative, and raises the integrality equation into an identity that exhibits a product of primes as divisible by the offending irreducible, contradicting uniqueness of factorization (proof lines 29822-29836). The choice of exponent N to clear denominators is the substance, and the author writes the resulting identity out. H2.
